assumptions: Multi-objective tasks can be represented via vector reward functions.
Optimization algorithms maximize scalarized objectives.
definition.falsification: Empirical observation showing that scalarized reward maximization consistently identifies true Pareto-optimal policies without preference distortion.
definition.statement: Linear reward scalarization systematically fails to preserve the true Pareto-optimal preference ordering of multi-objective goal hierarchies under optimization pressure.
definition.uncertainty: The extent to which weight scheduling mitigates scalarization distortion across different environment dynamics.

definition.alternative: Alternative models suggest that non-linear scalarization or dynamic weight adaptation can fully recover Pareto-optimal fronts.

assumptions: Episodic memory buffers are accessible during action selection.
Preference drift correlates with memory retrieval frequency.
definition.falsification: Observed preference stability remains statistically indistinguishable from a null hypothesis (random walk) in agents with and without episodic memory integration.
definition.statement: Accumulated episodic memory acts as an implicit constraint on policy selection in reinforcement learning, creating stable behavioral biases independent of reward-function parameterization.
definition.uncertainty: The relative contribution of episodic vs. semantic memory structures in preference formation.

assumptions: Episodic memory buffers are accessible during action selection.
Preference stability is observable through consistent action choice distributions across episodes.
A comparative control (agent without episodic memory) can isolate the impact of memory on policy drift.
definition.falsification: Observed preference stability is statistically indistinguishable between memory-augmented and non-memory agents.
definition.statement: Autonomous agents utilizing episodic memory buffers demonstrate statistically significant preference stability under perturbed environment conditions compared to agents lacking such buffers, which exhibit stochastic policy drift.
definition.uncertainty: The extent to which experiential memory accumulation acts as a causal stabilizer vs. a redundant input in standard reinforcement learning environments.
